blocks.text: 插件化、运行时中立的日志库——核心只有 200 多行，级别过滤、彩色控制台输出、批量上报、HTTP 发送、进程退出兜底、流式 AI 输出这些具体能力全部是可选插件。

大部分日志库要么"太薄"（只有 `console.log` 的包装，加个级别过滤就要自己写），要么"太厚"（内置一大堆你用不上的传输器、格式化器，想自定义还得绕过它的既有设计）。`@migaia/logger` 走的是第三条路：核心只负责"一条日志从产生到落地"这条最短路径本身——构造 entry、跑一遍处理管线（pipeline）、分发给若干个输出端（sink）、收尾时等待异步工作完成（flush/shutdown）——不内置"级别""颜色""批量"这些概念，这些全部通过插件注入。

这个设计带来一个直接的好处：你不需要的能力，一行代码都不会进你的 bundle。只要 `level()` 和 `color()`，产物就只有级别过滤和控制台着色两个插件的体积；生产环境加上 `http()` 和 `batch()`，日志会自动攒批发到你的日志平台；进程退出前需要保证日志不丢，加一个 `process()`。整个库基于 `@migaia/plugin-host` 构建，插件的安装、卸载、生命周期管理都复用同一套经过充分打磨的机制。

blocks.text: 不适合的场景：如果你只是想要一个"能设置级别的 `console.log`"，`level()` + 原生 `console` 可能就够了，不需要理解插件系统。

items: console 风格调用体验：`log.info('user %s logged in', userId)`，参数就是参数，不强制你写结构化对象。
需要结构化时也能结构化：`log.dispatchRaw({ tag, message, meta, data, context })` 一次性给全字段，适合审计日志、结构化上报。
收尾保证：`flush()` 会等待所有已知的异步输出（sink 返回的 Promise、批处理、转发下游）完成；`shutdown()` 在此基础上先跑你注册的收尾钩子，再彻底关闭。
失败不打断业务：sink 抛错、pipeline 抛错、flush 抛错，都不会从你调用 `log.info()` 的那一行抛出来——通过 `onFailure()` 单独观察，业务代码永远不会因为日志系统出问题而崩溃。
多目标转发：一次 `extends(otherLogger)` 就能让当前 logger 的每条日志完整走一遍目标 logger 自己的 pipeline 和 sink（包括目标自己的级别过滤），而不是简单的抄送。
HTTP 上报开箱即用：内置重试、超时、429 退避、批量攒批，不用自己写这套基础设施。
运行时中立：核心不 import `process`、不依赖 DOM，缺失能力时优雅降级（比如浏览器没有 `process`，`raw()` 自动退回 `console.log`）。

blocks.code:
import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { color, level } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  context: ['api'],
  plugins: [level({ level: 'info' }), color({ format: 'pretty', color: 'auto' })]
})

log.info('server listening on %d', 3000)
log.error('request failed', new Error('timeout'))

await log.flush() // 确保上面这些日志真正落地了再退出/继续

blocks.code:
import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { batch, http, level, process } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [
    level({ level: 'info' }),
    batch({ maxSize: 50, maxWaitMs: 1000 }),
    http({ url: 'https://logs.example/v1/entries', batch: { maxSize: 50 } }),
    process() // 进程退出/崩溃前自动 flush
  ]
})

log.onFailure(({ source, error }) => console.error(`[logger] ${source} failed`, error))

blocks.text: 1. 构造函数只接受同步安装的插件。`new Logger({ plugins: [...] })` 里的插件必须能同步完成安装，需要异步安装的插件用 `await log.use(plugin)`。 2. 插件实例不能跨 logger 复用。每次安装都应该重新调用一次插件工厂函数（`level()`、`http()` 等），不要把同一个插件实例装到多个 `Logger`，否则内部状态可能串联。 3. `shutdown()` 之后日志被静默忽略，不会抛错也不会有任何提示——这是有意的（避免退出流程里到处加判断），需要感知的话订阅 `onFailure()` 或自行检查状态。 4. 日志系统内部的失败不会从业务调用抛出。`log.info()` 永远不会因为 sink 挂了而抛异常——务必用 `onFailure()` 观察，否则问题会悄悄消失。 5. `pipeline.mode` 构造后不可切换。sync stage 可提升到任意模式，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其余不兼容组合会立即报 `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`，详见 USEGUIDE。 6. `http()` 通过 Feature 解析 batch provider：同批 `[batch(), http(...)]` 或反序均按依赖排序；跨调用晚装 batch 不会追溯重绑。 7. `extends()` 只转发运行时输出路径，不会把目标 logger 的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并进当前变量的类型。 8. 批处理队列有界且不会静默丢日志：`maxPendingBatches` 默认 `1024`，满载时抛出/上报 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；生产环境应通过 `onFailure()` 监控并在下游恢复后再接纳新日志。

sections.heading: 9. 高阶组合示例 · 失败隔离、批量上报与确定性关闭

blocks.text: 生产日志链路既不能让上报失败打断业务，也不能在进程退出时丢掉已经接纳的批次。把失败观察器、批处理和 HTTP sink 安装在同一个 Logger 上，并在宿主关闭边界显式等待 `shutdown()`：
`batch()` 必须位于 `http()` 前面，才能让 HTTP sink 使用批量调度。`onFailure()` 是日志基础设施失败的观察出口；业务日志调用不会替它抛错。并发或重入的 `shutdown()` 共享同一个进行中的关闭 Promise，因此宿主的多个收尾入口可以安全汇合，但终态 Logger 不能重新启用，需要创建新实例。
完整构造选项、全部 API 精确签名、pipeline 四种模式的执行顺序差异、每个内置插件的完整配置项、`flush`/`shutdown` 的精确语义与边界情况、自定义 runtime manager（替换底层能力用于测试/特殊宿主）、以及更多组合示例，见 USEGUIDE.md。

Pipeline replacements must retain a current-realm `Date` in `entry.time`. An invalid replacement (including serialized timestamps or a foreign-realm Date) reports `PIPELINE_ENTRY_INVALID` through `onFailure` with source `pipeline`, then delivers the original entry. Dispatch remains non-throwing.

`new Logger({ execution, runtimeManager })` captures that host capability owner. If omitted, construction captures the current module default. Built-in console, UUID, HTTP and file plugins use their logger's owner. `createAbortController` is an optional host cancellation factory for alternate AbortSignal implementations; HTTP falls back to native controllers when it is absent. This is the same cancellation boundary in production and tests.

`setLoggerRuntimeManager` now selects the default for future instances; it no longer retargets existing loggers. Migrate code that changes a live logger globally to construct it with an explicit `runtimeManager`. The manager object itself is retained by reference. ProcessPlugin still owns one shared set of exit/signal hooks: all participants must agree on process identity, configuration and scheduler domain, or receive `PLUGIN_CONFIG_CONFLICT`. Its late diagnostics use the first installer's captured manager.
批次过载会报告 BATCH_OVERFLOW，并丢最老排队批次；若容量全被在途批次占用，则丢新批次。关闭先排空 HTTP 最终日志，再在插件释放时取消剩余传输，cleanupComplete 不等于送达回执。

颜色/级别类型统一从根入口使用 ILoggerColorMode/ILoggerLevel，移除 plugins 的 IColorMode/ILogLevel；ILoggerDomainCore 是内部 Host 装配类型，公开调用方使用 ILoggerCore/ILoggerPluginCore。实例 dispose() 与 shutdown(manual) 返回相同的稳定 Promise<IPluginHostDisposalResult>，包括失败结果；时钟失败也进入该完成 Promise 并尝试宿主清理。
本文是 `@migaia/logger` 的应用与适配器参考手册。先看 README.md 的五分钟上手示例，跑起来之后再回来查这里的细节——README 讲“是什么、为什么用、5 分钟怎么跑起来”，本文覆盖公开运行时 API、配置项和边界行为；仅供插件泛型推导的 type-only helper 由发布的 `.d.ts` 与编辑器提示承载。

`pipeline.mode` 在构造时确定，之后不能切换：

stage 可以等待异步工作，`async (value, next) => void`
通过生成器组合处理流程
terminal 语义与 `generator` 一致，串行 `await` 耗尽每个 stage（中间 yield 不提前进入下一 stage）

blocks.text: `useAsyncGeneratorPipeline` 由 LoggerCore 显式委派给唯一的功能 Host（Logger 不继承 PluginHost），能力与 `@migaia/plugin-host` 的 `host.useAsyncGeneratorPipeline` 完全一致，用法见该包文档。
内置同步插件复用 Host 的模式适配。直接注册 stage 时，同步 `usePipeline` 可用于全部 mode，generator 还可提升到 async-generator；其它异步/生成器 stage 要求相应模式。不兼容方法在具体 mode 类型中为 never，运行时也拒绝；不要求所有注册方法名与 mode 完全相同。

pipeline 执行期间禁止新增 stage，避免修改一条正在执行中的处理链。每个 stage 在一次调用里最多调用一次 `next()`：重复调用抛出 `PIPELINE_NEXT_DUPLICATE`；stage 已经返回后才延迟调用 `next()` 会产生 `PIPELINE_NEXT_LATE` diagnostic（不抛错，只上报）；完全不调用 `next()` 表示这个 stage 主动拦截了这条 entry，不会继续往下传递。四种 mode 使用完全相同的违规检测逻辑。

`sync` 模式是扁平转换管道：`next()` 只是记录下一个值，下游 stage 在当前 stage 返回之后才执行。`async` 模式是洋葱模型：`await next(value)` 会等待整条下游链跑完才继续，因此当前 stage 可以在 `next()` 之后写"后置逻辑"，并且这段逻辑能感知下游是否已经处理完毕。`async-generator` 既不是洋葱模型也不是流式管道，是"stage 顺序执行、每个 stage 各自异步跑完取一个终值"，介于 `async` 与 `generator` 之间。这个差异是切换 pipeline mode 时最容易踩的坑。

应用侧的 `log.config` 委托给 Plugin Host：`get('plugin')` 可读整份插件配置，`get('plugin.key')` 读取嵌套值，`get('plugin.[index].key')` 读取数组项；`update(name, recipe)` 浅合并 patch 后提交新的所有权快照。配置中的对象和数组递归冻结，读取方不得修改；使用 update 返回 patch。
插件在 `install(core)` 里拿到的 `core.config` 刻意更窄：它只有无参的 `get()`，只能读取当前插件自己的配置快照，不能通过这个门面读取或更新其他插件的配置。插件的异步生命周期也不应该通过反复轮询自己的 config 来等待某个外部条件——这不是配置系统设计的用途。

sections.heading: 6. 插件安装与实例所有权

blocks.text: 构造参数里的插件按数组顺序同步安装。任一插件安装失败，构造函数直接抛出，并触发已登记资源的回滚（这部分机制来自 `@migaia/plugin-host`，逐插件回滚见其文档）；返回 Promise 或 thenable 的 `install()` 同样会被视为失败。需要异步安装能力的插件，在 Logger 构造完成后使用 `await log.use(plugin)`，并妥善处理 rejected Promise。
一个插件对象只归属一次安装。不要把同一个 `http()`、`reasoning()`、`color()` 或其他有状态插件的实例装到多个 Logger 上——每次安装都应该重新调用一次对应的工厂函数。否则该插件内部创建的 controller、buffer、配置快照、disposer 等状态可能在多个 Logger 实例之间相互串联，产生难以定位的 bug。

等待本 logger 已经观察到的 deferred task、异步 sink 结果、`onFlush` handler、批处理与 extends 下游全部完成。内部有一个约 3 秒的预算：每一轮 drain 都会和"剩余预算"做一次race——如果某个被追踪的 Promise 迟迟不 settle（比如一个卡死的 HTTP 请求），`flush()` 最多等到预算耗尽就会返回，不会被单个永不 resolve 的 Promise 永久卡住，剩余未完成的工作会在通过 `onFailure()` 上报一条"flush deadline reached"之后，留给后续的 `flush()` 调用继续等待。
`flush()` 会追踪任何"看起来像 Promise"的返回值（不要求严格是当前 realm 的 `Promise` 实例），一个手写的、跨 iframe/VM 的 thenable 对象同样会被正确等待。

`shutdown()` 先原子性地进入关闭流程（同步标记状态并发布一个内部 promise），再依次执行 shutdown handler——handler 内部仍然可以通过 `log()`/`dispatchRaw()` 写收尾日志，这些日志会被后续的 flush 阶段一并等到。`raw()` 从关闭流程开始那一刻起就不再直接写 stdout。收尾钩子跑完后进入 flush，再卸载全部插件，最终进入终态，新日志被静默忽略。

并发/重入调用 `shutdown()` 会 alias 到同一个进行中的 Promise——即便某个 shutdown handler 自己又调用了一次 `shutdown()`，也只会拿到当前这一轮已经在进行的同一个 Promise，不会触发第二轮独立的 handler 遍历。`shutdown()` 失败（比如某个插件的 `dispose()` 抛错）时，实例会被标记为终态并停止接收日志——这不是一个可以重试恢复的中间状态；后续调用始终返回同一个 Promise，保留其结果或拒绝。结果是宿主 IPluginHostDisposalResult：cleanupErrors/cleanupComplete 描述物理清理，不代表日志已送达；拒绝也不会再次重试关闭。时钟读取失败进入该 Promise 的 INVALID_OPTION/cause，仍尝试宿主清理，附带清理失败不会替换主因。

log.log('info', 'user updated', userId) // userId 是 console 参数
log.dispatchRaw({
  tag: 'info',

  meta: { userId },

  context: ['api', 'users']

blocks.text: `ILogEntry` 完整字段：`id`、`tag`、`time`、`message`、`args`、`meta`、`context`、`error`、`data`。传入的 `Error` 参数会生成一份可序列化的 `error` 投影（`name`/`message`/`stack`），同时保留 `error.raw` 指向原始 `Error` 对象的引用。

Hook 名称约定：`before`、`after`、`before:<tag>`、`after:<tag>`，也可以用任意自定义字符串。`before`/`after` 系列 hook 拿到的是活引用的 entry——pipeline 阶段本来就需要能修改 entry 内容，这是有意的行为，不是隔离没做好；只有进入每个 sink 之前，核心才会复制一份顶层容器（`args`、`meta`、`context`、`data`、`time` 各自浅拷贝一层），因此 sink 之间互不干扰，也不会看到 hook 后续可能产生的修改。反过来说：如果一个 `after` hook 修改了 `entry.data`，这个修改不会反映到已经拿到快照的 sink 上，但会反映到随后 `extends()` 转发出去的下游（因为转发发生在 `after` hook 之后）——利用这个时序差异做数据脱敏/补充时需要注意先后顺序。嵌套的业务对象（比如 `meta` 里挂的一个对象引用）在浅拷贝之后仍然是同一个引用，sink 不应该修改它们。
添加 `debug`、`info`、`warn`、`error`、`fatal`、`setLevel(level)`、`addFilter(filter)`、`removeFilter(filter)`。

rows: 全部 `(entry) => boolean` 返回 true 才放行。
该插件产生的日志是否走 `defer` 异步输出。

pretty 格式是否包含 ISO 时间戳。

blocks.text: `color` 会识别 `entry.data.silent === true` 并跳过打印这条 entry（但其他 sink，比如 HTTP，仍会正常接收它）——常用于"这条日志需要上报但不需要刷屏"的场景。
不添加任何 logger 方法，只提供 shared 能力 `createBatcher(config, onBatch)`，供其他插件（如 `http()`）复用。

批次里第一项进入后的最长等待时间。
同时执行的批次数；必须是正安全整数。
排队中与执行中的批次总上限；满载时报告 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；优先丢最老排队批次，若全在执行则丢新批次。
满批次的回调是否走 `defer` 调度。

blocks.text: Batcher 的 `push(item)` 收集条目，`flush()` 发送剩余条目并等待正在进行的回调完成；这个 batcher 会自动登记进宿主 Logger 的 `flush()` 追踪范围，不需要手动接入。
把 entry 以 `POST { entries }` 的形式发送到指定 endpoint。

rows: 网络错误、429、5xx 情况下的额外重试次数。
单次请求最长等待时间；超时会 abort 当前请求并按网络错误处理。
覆盖传给 `batch()` shared factory 的配置。

blocks.text: 4xx 错误（429 除外）会直接失败、不重试；429 优先读取响应的 `Retry-After` 头部作为等待时间，没有该头部时退回指数退避。关闭先排空最终日志，再在 HTTP 插件释放时 abort 剩余请求；失败由 `onFailure()` 观察。同一批安装的 batch/http 按 Feature 依赖排序，`[http(...), batch()]` 同样生效；跨 use 调用晚装 provider 不会追溯重绑。没有 batch provider 时，指定 http.batch 仍启用本地有界队列，但强制 maxSize:1、asyncOutput:false。

`file` 只从 `@migaia/logger/plugins/file` 导入，不经根入口。它把每批 entry 写成逐行 JSON；`batch` 复用现有批处理器配置，`rotate.maxEntries`/`rotate.maxBytes` 在单批达到阈值时调用可选的 `fs.rotate(path)`。Node 条件默认动态加载 `node:fs/promises` 做 append；浏览器/default 条件只接受 `setLoggerRuntimeManager()` 注入的 `fs.append(path, text)`，没有能力时安装失败，原始 `FILE_SINK_UNAVAILABLE` 可从 PluginHost 安装错误的 `cause` 读取。写入失败走 `onFailure()`，不会从普通 `log()` 调用栈抛出。

blocks.code:
import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { file } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/file'

const logger = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [file({ path: 'logs/app.jsonl', batch: { maxSize: 20 } })]
})
logger.log('info', 'ready')
await logger.flush()
await logger.shutdown('manual')

blocks.text: Node/Bun 风格的进程适配器，运行时环境没有 `process` 全局对象时自动变成 no-op，不会报错。

rows: 捕获 `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` 并记录为 fatal 日志。
收到信号/崩溃/正常 exit 时，最长允许的 drain 时间。
在 `process.exit()` 真正执行前发起一次 flush；这会改变 `process.exit()` 原本同步立即退出的语义，谨慎开启。

blocks.text: 同一个运行时的底层监听器只会注册一次（多个 logger 都装 `process()` 不会重复挂多份监听器）；最后一个安装该插件的 logger 被卸载后，监听器和内部 shutdown 状态都会正确清理，因此这个插件可以安全地反复装卸。

添加 `startThinking`、`thinking`、`endThinking`、`startResponse`、`response`、`endResponse`。逐 token 内容通过 `raw()` 直接输出（不经过 pipeline）；每个阶段结束时会额外生成一条 `data.silent = true` 的完整 entry，方便 HTTP/审计类 sink 收集完整内容而不重复打印到控制台。

rows: 流式输出与收尾完整 entry 是否走异步调度。

blocks.text: 安装在 `color()` 之后可以复用它的 `paint`/`dim` shared 能力做染色；没装 `color()` 时自动退化为纯文本输出。
为每一条经过 pipeline 的 entry 写入 `data.uuid` 和 `data.uuidDisplay`。

rows: 是否让 `color()` 的 pretty/JSON 输出里展示这个 UUID。

blocks.text: `extends()` 转发的是完整的处理路径，不是简单抄送——目标 logger 自己的级别阈值、过滤器同样会对转发过来的日志生效。转发时会把当前 `topic` 追加进一份仅用于展示的 `topicChain`，同时把当前 logger 的 `id` 追加进一份仅用于循环检测的内部路径（两者故意分开维护：循环检测不能依赖可能为空、可能重名的 `topic` 字符串）。`extends()` 注册时会做一次静态循环检测（`a.extends(b); b.extends(a)` 这种直接循环会在调用 `extends()` 那一刻就抛错），转发时还有运行时兜底检测，防止通过外部自定义的 `ILoggerCore` 实现绕过静态检测形成循环转发。
不再需要某条转发边时调用 `api.unextend(audit)`。它按目标 logger 的稳定 context id 移除关系；至少移除一条返回 `true`，目标不存在或重复移除返回 `false`，不会关闭目标 logger。
`extends()` 只组合运行时的日志输出路径，不会把目标 logger 通过插件获得的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并到当前变量的类型上——如果 `audit` 装了 `level()` 有 `.info()` 方法，`api` 不会因为 `extends(audit)` 而在类型上获得任何新方法。extends 关系图不允许成环；`flush()` 会沿着这个图等待全部下游完成。
测试环境、非标准宿主，或者需要替换底层能力实现时，可以整体替换 runtime manager：

`getLoggerRuntimeManager()` 返回当前活动 manager 的同一引用，适合在适配器安装前读取或做能力探测；不要修改返回对象。`setLoggerRuntimeManager` 返回一个幂等恢复函数，支持嵌套调用（后进先出恢复），适合在测试用例的 `beforeEach`/`afterEach` 里成对使用。`LoggerLevel`、`LoggerColorMode`、`LoggerReasoningPhase`、`LoggerStatus` 是稳定状态常量，`LOGGER_SOURCE` 是错误身份的稳定 source；比较时应引用这些导出，不要散写字符串。

blocks.code:
import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { batch, color, http, level, process, uuid } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  context: ['worker'],
  plugins: [
    level({ level: 'info' }),
    uuid({ display: true }),
    batch({ maxSize: 50, maxWaitMs: 1000 }),
    http({ url: 'https://logs.example/v1/entries', batch: { maxSize: 50 } }),
    color({ format: 'pretty' }),
    process()
  ]
})

log.onFailure(({ source, error }) => reportLoggerFailure(source, error))
log.info('job started', { jobId: 'j_1' })
await log.flush()

blocks.text: 所有 Logger 自有错误都带 `source: '@migaia/logger'` 与下列稳定 `code`；业务日志入口通常不直接抛出 sink/plugin 失败，应通过 `onFailure()` 观察。

rows: 公开配置不可读或结构非法；修正配置，getter 原错误保留在 `cause`
pipeline 替换值的 time 非当前 realm Date；报告后交付原 entry

非成功响应或可重试传输耗尽；检查 endpoint/网络并由业务决定补偿
retries 不是有限非负整数；构造前修正

sections.heading: 13. 构建、测试与常见问题排查

blocks.text: 在仓库根目录运行以下包级门禁；`test` 会先执行本包的 `build`。

blocks.code:
pnpm --filter @migaia/logger fmt
pnpm --filter @migaia/logger lint
pnpm --filter @migaia/logger typecheck
pnpm --filter @migaia/logger typecheck:test
pnpm --filter @migaia/logger test

blocks.text: Q：日志明明报错了，但业务代码里 catch 不到。 这是设计如此——日志系统内部的失败不会从 `log()`/`dispatchRaw()` 抛出，避免日志问题拖垮业务逻辑。用 `log.onFailure(fn)` 接入监控，`fn` 会收到 `{ source, error }`，`source` 取值包括 `defer`/`hook`/`sink`/`pipeline`/`flush`/`forward`/`shutdown`。
Q：`flush()` 迟迟不返回。 检查是否有 sink/hook 返回了一个永远不会 settle 的 Promise——`flush()` 内部有约 3 秒预算会自动放弃并通过 `onFailure` 报告，但如果你观察到的等待时间远超 3 秒，说明可能是别的原因（比如递归触发了新的 `defer` 任务）。
Q：`shutdown()` 之后还想恢复使用。 不支持——`shutdown()`（无论成功还是失败）都会把 logger 带入终态，之后的日志调用会被静默忽略。需要"可恢复"的场景应该创建一个新的 `Logger` 实例，而不是复用已经 shutdown 的实例。
Q：批量 HTTP 发送没生效，还是一条一条发。 检查 batch provider 是否与 http 同批安装（该批按 Feature 依赖排序）或已提前安装；跨调用晚装 batch 不会重新绑定已安装的 http。
Q：同一个插件装在两个 Logger 上，行为很奇怪。 不要复用插件实例，见 §6。每次安装都重新调用一次插件工厂函数（比如两次分别调用 `http({...})`，而不是把同一个 `http({...})` 的返回值装两次）。
Q：TypeScript 提示某个插件方法不存在。 构造参数中静态安装的插件扩展出现在实例类型上；`await log.use(plugin)` 返回输入顺序的 handle tuple，动态扩展通过 handle.extensions 调用，原 log 变量不会扩张。

Pipeline replacements must retain a current-realm `Date` in `entry.time`. An invalid replacement (including serialized timestamps or a foreign-realm Date) reports `PIPELINE_ENTRY_INVALID` through `onFailure` with source `pipeline`, then delivers the original entry. Dispatch remains non-throwing.

`new Logger({ execution, runtimeManager })` captures that host capability owner. If omitted, construction captures the current module default. Built-in console, UUID, HTTP and file plugins use their logger's owner. `createAbortController` is an optional host cancellation factory for alternate AbortSignal implementations; HTTP falls back to native controllers when it is absent. This is the same cancellation boundary in production and tests.

`setLoggerRuntimeManager` now selects the default for future instances; it no longer retargets existing loggers. Migrate code that changes a live logger globally to construct it with an explicit `runtimeManager`. The manager object itself is retained by reference. ProcessPlugin still owns one shared set of exit/signal hooks: all participants must agree on process identity, configuration and scheduler domain, or receive `PLUGIN_CONFIG_CONFLICT`. Its late diagnostics use the first installer's captured manager.
公开面收敛：颜色与级别类型统一从根入口导入 `ILoggerColorMode`、`ILoggerLevel`；plugins 不再导出 IColorMode/ILogLevel。Host 装配类型 ILoggerDomainCore 仅留内部，应用/插件使用 ILoggerCore/ILoggerPluginCore。

`hook()` 返回的 off 只移除本次登记，同一函数多次登记互不影响。forward 的 display topicChain 暴露在 sink 私有 data 快照中，循环检测 symbol 仍不外泄。HTTP 与 color JSON 输出使用 Utils 的有界错误链投影，保留 source/code/name/message/stack/cause/errors，且不发送 raw；本地 console/custom sink 仍保留原 Error 引用。原始业务错误没有 semantic identity 时，序列化采用 Utils 的 unknown/UNKNOWN 诊断占位，不将它伪称为包内抛错码。宿主 reporter 自身 throw/rejection 通过既有 host exception queue 可观察，不递归调用 logger reporter，也不替换业务结果。

symbols.purpose: Core capabilities of a logger, also passed to plugins as `core` in `install(core)` (without `use` / `unUse`).
symbols.core:
config: Configuration store of the installed plugins. On a logger it is `ILoggerConfig` (`get(path)`, `update(name, recipe)`); inside a plugin `install(core)` it is a reader of that plugin configuration only (`get()`).
ctx: Frozen context of this logger: `id`, application `options`, default context `path`, `topic`, `createdAt` and `env`.
scheduler: Clock and timers used by `flush()`, `shutdown()` and batch deadlines; the `scheduler` option or `systemScheduler`.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs) captured at construction from the `runtimeManager` option or `getLoggerRuntimeManager()`; plugins use the same object.
log: Console-style entry point: builds an entry with this tag and message and dispatches it through pipeline, hooks and sinks. A trailing object stays an argument; it is not turned into `meta`. Never throws for sink failures.
log.tag: Entry tag such as `info` or `audit`; `level()` filters standard level tags.
log.message: Message text; `%s`, `%d`, `%o` placeholders are left for the console sink.
log.args: Extra values stored in `entry.args` in order.
No value. Shutdown handlers can still enqueue final structured entries; calls are ignored after draining closes dispatch admission.
dispatchRaw: Dispatches an entry with explicit fields (`meta`, `data`, `context`, `error`, `time`) for structured or audit logs.
dispatchRaw.input: `{ tag, message, args?, meta?, data?, context?, error?, time? }`; `context` defaults to the `context` option.
dispatchRaw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing; failures go to `onFailure()`.
raw: Writes text straight to stdout (or `console.log` without `process`), skipping pipeline and sinks; used for streaming output. Ignored once shutdown starts.
raw.text: Text passed unchanged to runtimeManager.write. A host stdout writer can preserve no-newline output; the default console.log fallback without process adds its own newline.
raw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing.
usePipeline: Registers a synchronous stage (entry, next, context?) => void in every pipeline mode. PluginHost lifts it into the selected mode; call next(entry) to continue or omit next to drop the entry.
usePipeline.stage: The stage function; call `next` at most once.
The same logger for chaining; synchronous registration works in all modes. Other stage registration methods follow the mode compatibility matrix.
useAsyncPipeline: Registers an async onion-style stage (mode `async` only): code after `await next(entry)` runs once the downstream finished.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (entry, next) => void`.
The same logger; other modes reject it at type level and at runtime.
useGeneratorPipeline: Registers a generator stage (modes `generator` and `async-generator`).
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: Generator (entry, context?), with optional pipeline context as the second argument, never next. Return a payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE after yielding to continue; an implicit undefined return halts.
The same logger, for chaining.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Registers an async generator stage (mode `async-generator` only); each stage runs to its final value before the next.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: Async generator (entry, context?) with optional context as the second argument. Yield stores a candidate; return payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE to continue. The logger explicitly delegates stage registration to its functional Host.
useSink: Registers an output that receives every entry passing the pipeline. Each sink gets its own shallow copy; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`; a throw goes to `onFailure()` with source `sink`.
useSink.sink: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`.
A function that removes only this registration; calling it again does nothing.
hook: Registers a hook under a name: built-in `before`, `after`, `before:<tag>`, `after:<tag>`, or a name a plugin fires. Hooks receive the live entry and may change it.
hook.name: Hook name.
hook.fn: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`.
An idempotent off callback removing only this registration; registering the same function again creates an independent subscription.
fireHook: Runs every hook registered under `name` with the given entry now.
fireHook.name: Hook name to fire.
fireHook.entry: An entry, usually received in a sink or stage.
Nothing; hook failures go to `onFailure()`.
onFailure: Observes failures of sinks, hooks, pipeline, deferred tasks, flush, forwarding and shutdown. Logging calls never throw them, so register this in production. If the terminal runtime reporter throws, rejects or has a throwing then getter, the existing Utils host exception queue exposes that failure without recursion or changing the business result.
onFailure.fn: `({ source, error }) => void`; see `ILogFailure`.
defer: Runs a task after the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager; `flush()` and `shutdown()` wait for it.
defer.task: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
Nothing; the task is scheduled, not awaited.
onFlush: Registers a callback that empties a buffer on every `flush()`.
onFlush.fn: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
flush: Waits for deferred tasks, async sink results, `onFlush` callbacks, batches and forwarded loggers. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a stuck Promise is abandoned after about 3 seconds and reported with `LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE`.
Resolves when the known work finished or the budget ran out.
onShutdown: Registers a cleanup handler run at the start of `shutdown()`; it may still write final logs.
onShutdown.fn: `(reason) => void | Promise<void>`; `reason` is the value passed to `shutdown()`.
shutdown: Closes the logger: runs shutdown handlers, flushes, then uninstalls all plugins. Reentrant and concurrent calls share the same Promise. Afterwards logs are silently ignored and the logger cannot be reopened.
shutdown.reason: Why it closes: `manual` from application code; `signal`, `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection` are passed by `process()`.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult` from `@migaia/plugin-host`; `cleanupErrors` lists plugin cleanup failures. A clock failure rejects this same published completion after attempting Host cleanup, retaining primary and cleanup causes. Persistent clock failure can also defeat the Host budget; cleanup or receipt success does not promise remote delivery.
dispose: Same as `shutdown("manual")`.
The disposal result of `shutdown()`.
use: Installs plugins after construction (also async ones), through the same checks as constructor plugins. Each call must use new plugin objects.
use.plugins: Plugin objects created by factories such as `level()` or `http(config)`.
A tuple of plugin handles in input order; `handle.extensions` holds the API the plugin added.
unUse: Uninstalls a plugin by name and releases what it registered (stages, sinks, hooks, flush and shutdown callbacks).
unUse.name: Plugin name, such as `LEVEL_PLUGIN_NAME` (`level`).
Resolves after the plugin is removed.
extends: Forwards every entry, after this logger processed it, through the whole pipeline and sinks of each target (their level filters apply). Self or cyclic forwarding throws `EXTENDS_SELF` / `EXTENDS_CYCLE`.
extends.others: Target loggers created by `new Logger()`.
This logger, for chaining.
unextend: Removes forwarding edges to the given loggers; the targets are not closed.
unextend.others: Loggers previously passed to `extends()`.
`true` when at least one edge was removed.
onDispose: Inside a plugin `install(core)` only: registers a cleanup run when the plugin is uninstalled.
onDispose.resource: A disposer function or an object with `dispose()`.
Nothing; the cleanup is registered.

members.name: config
members.description: Plugins read their own configuration through `core.config.get<TConfig>()`, not `this.config`. This scoped reader exposes the host-owned snapshot without a plugin-name argument. Keeping reads at the core boundary makes plugin configuration available to host diagnostics.

members.name: ctx
members.description: Read-only context containers. See `ILoggerContext` for the mutability boundary.

members.name: scheduler
members.description: The logger's monotonic clock source (R-9). `flush`, `shutdown`, batch deadlines, and `boundedWait` use this scheduler. Defaults to utils/scheduler `systemScheduler`. Plugins use it to share the host's clock domain.

members.name: runtimeManager
members.description: Host capabilities captured by this logger; plugins share the same instance owner.

members.name: log
members.signature: log(tag: string, message: string, ...args: unknown[]): void;
members.description: Synchronously constructs and dispatches an entry. Use `dispatchRaw` scheduling options for asynchronous output.

members.name: dispatchRaw
members.description: Dispatches explicit entry fields such as `meta`, `data`, and `context`.

members.name: usePipeline
members.description: Registers a pipeline stage that can transform an entry, forward it with `next`, or drop it by omitting `next`. Supported methods follow the middleware-pipeline promotion table. Sync stages run in any mode. Generator stages also promote to `async-generator`. Other stages require their matching mode. An unresolved mode union retains all methods and leaves validation to runtime admission.

members.name: useSink
members.description: Registers a sink. Every registered sink processes entries that pass the full pipeline, such as console and HTTP sinks together.

members.name: hook
members.description: Registers a named lifecycle hook. Built-in names are `before`, `after`, `before:${tag}`, and `after:${tag}`. Plugins can also define their own hook names.

members.name: onFailure
members.description: Observes asynchronous output failures without changing normal log-call control flow.

members.name: defer
members.description: Schedules work outside the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager. `flush` and `shutdown` wait for this work. Plugins configured for async output use this path for rendering, stdout writes, or network requests.

members.name: onFlush
members.description: Registers a callback to empty a buffer during `flush()`. The core invokes these callbacks and also waits for unfinished `defer()` tasks and Promises returned by sinks. For example, an HTTP sink without batching still keeps each pending request in the drain wait.

members.name: onShutdown
members.description: Shutdown disposes installed plugins after draining; subsequent log calls are ignored.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Returns the same terminal completion as shutdown(manual).

members.name: use
members.signature: use<const NewP extends readonly ILoggerPluginConstraint[]>(...plugins: NewP): Promise<IPluginHandleTuple<NewP>>;
members.description: Installs plugins on an existing logger through the same host admission path used by constructor installation. Duplicate plugin names, extension conflicts, and dependency cycles are rejected by that host. Providers declare Feature names. Returns a Promise of plugin handles, preserving each plugin's extension types on its handle. The existing logger variable does not gain new TypeScript methods.

members.name: unUse
members.description: Removes an installed plugin by name through the owning host and releases its registered resources. This includes pipeline stages, sinks, hooks, flush callbacks, shutdown callbacks, and plugin extensions. Missing plugin names reject with `PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLED`. Required Feature dependents can block removal.

members.name: raw
members.description: Writes raw text to stdout without passing through the pipeline or sinks. `asyncOutput: true` schedules the write through `defer`. Streaming plugins such as reasoning use this for token output without a complete log format per token.

members.name: extends
members.signature: extends(...others: readonly Omit<ILoggerCore<TMode, TShared>, 'config' | 'onDispose'>[]): ILoggerCore<TMode, TShared>;
members.description: Forwards entries to the full pipelines and sinks of each target after the current logger processes them. After `log1.extends(log2, log3)`, target level thresholds and filters still apply to forwarded entries. Each forwarding hop records its topic in internal forwarding state carried in `entry.data`. Registration detects cycles using logger context IDs. Runtime forwarding also skips IDs already present in the internal forwarding path. This composes forwarding behavior, not plugin extension types. The returned logger keeps the current logger's TypeScript capabilities; target-only methods are not added.

members.name: unextend
members.description: Removes named extension edges; returns true when at least one edge was removed.

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Core capabilities of a logger, also passed to plugins as `core` in `install(core)` (without `use` / `unUse`).

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import ILoggerCore from @migaia/logger, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 适用场景
sections.content: Use ILoggerCore when its type contract and declared inputs match the result you need. Choose a different public symbol when ILoggerCore does not match the required inputs or return contract.

ctx: Frozen context of this logger: `id`, application `options`, default context `path`, `topic`, `createdAt` and `env`.
scheduler: Clock and timers used by `flush()`, `shutdown()` and batch deadlines; the `scheduler` option or `systemScheduler`.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs) captured at construction from the `runtimeManager` option or `getLoggerRuntimeManager()`; plugins use the same object.

log.message: Message text; `%s`, `%d`, `%o` placeholders are left for the console sink.

No value. Shutdown handlers can still enqueue final structured entries; calls are ignored after draining closes dispatch admission.

symbols.name: ILoggerPluginCore
symbols.signature: export type ILoggerPluginCore<TMode extends IPipelineConfig['mode'] = IMiddlewarePipelineMode, TShared extends Record<string, unknown> = Record<string, never>> = Omit<ILoggerCore<TMode, TShared>, 'use' | 'unUse' | 'onDispose'> & { onDispose(resource: import('@migaia/plugin-host').IPluginResource): void; };
symbols.purpose: The `core` a plugin receives in `install(core)`: the logger core without `use` / `unUse`, plus `onDispose()` for cleanup.
symbols.core:
config: Configuration store of the installed plugins. On a logger it is `ILoggerConfig` (`get(path)`, `update(name, recipe)`); inside a plugin `install(core)` it is a reader of that plugin configuration only (`get()`).
ctx: Frozen context of this logger: `id`, application `options`, default context `path`, `topic`, `createdAt` and `env`.
scheduler: Clock and timers used by `flush()`, `shutdown()` and batch deadlines; the `scheduler` option or `systemScheduler`.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs) captured at construction from the `runtimeManager` option or `getLoggerRuntimeManager()`; plugins use the same object.
log: Console-style entry point: builds an entry with this tag and message and dispatches it through pipeline, hooks and sinks. A trailing object stays an argument; it is not turned into `meta`. Never throws for sink failures.
log.tag: Entry tag such as `info` or `audit`; `level()` filters standard level tags.
log.message: Message text; `%s`, `%d`, `%o` placeholders are left for the console sink.
log.args: Extra values stored in `entry.args` in order.
No value. Shutdown handlers can still enqueue final structured entries; calls are ignored after draining closes dispatch admission.
dispatchRaw: Dispatches an entry with explicit fields (`meta`, `data`, `context`, `error`, `time`) for structured or audit logs.
dispatchRaw.input: `{ tag, message, args?, meta?, data?, context?, error?, time? }`; `context` defaults to the `context` option.
dispatchRaw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing; failures go to `onFailure()`.
raw: Writes text straight to stdout (or `console.log` without `process`), skipping pipeline and sinks; used for streaming output. Ignored once shutdown starts.
raw.text: Text passed unchanged to runtimeManager.write. A host stdout writer can preserve no-newline output; the default console.log fallback without process adds its own newline.
raw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing.
usePipeline: Registers a synchronous stage (entry, next, context?) => void in every pipeline mode. PluginHost lifts it into the selected mode; call next(entry) to continue or omit next to drop the entry.
usePipeline.stage: The stage function; call `next` at most once.
The same logger for chaining; synchronous registration works in all modes. Other stage registration methods follow the mode compatibility matrix.
useAsyncPipeline: Registers an async onion-style stage (mode `async` only): code after `await next(entry)` runs once the downstream finished.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (entry, next) => void`.
The same logger; other modes reject it at type level and at runtime.
useGeneratorPipeline: Registers a generator stage (modes `generator` and `async-generator`).
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: Generator (entry, context?), with optional pipeline context as the second argument, never next. Return a payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE after yielding to continue; an implicit undefined return halts.
The same logger, for chaining.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Registers an async generator stage (mode `async-generator` only); each stage runs to its final value before the next.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: Async generator (entry, context?) with optional context as the second argument. Yield stores a candidate; return payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE to continue. The logger explicitly delegates stage registration to its functional Host.
useSink: Registers an output that receives every entry passing the pipeline. Each sink gets its own shallow copy; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`; a throw goes to `onFailure()` with source `sink`.
useSink.sink: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`.
A function that removes only this registration; calling it again does nothing.
hook: Registers a hook under a name: built-in `before`, `after`, `before:<tag>`, `after:<tag>`, or a name a plugin fires. Hooks receive the live entry and may change it.
hook.name: Hook name.
hook.fn: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`.
An idempotent off callback removing only this registration; registering the same function again creates an independent subscription.
fireHook: Runs every hook registered under `name` with the given entry now.
fireHook.name: Hook name to fire.
fireHook.entry: An entry, usually received in a sink or stage.
Nothing; hook failures go to `onFailure()`.
onFailure: Observes failures of sinks, hooks, pipeline, deferred tasks, flush, forwarding and shutdown. Logging calls never throw them, so register this in production. If the terminal runtime reporter throws, rejects or has a throwing then getter, the existing Utils host exception queue exposes that failure without recursion or changing the business result.
onFailure.fn: `({ source, error }) => void`; see `ILogFailure`.
defer: Runs a task after the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager; `flush()` and `shutdown()` wait for it.
defer.task: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
Nothing; the task is scheduled, not awaited.
onFlush: Registers a callback that empties a buffer on every `flush()`.
onFlush.fn: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
flush: Waits for deferred tasks, async sink results, `onFlush` callbacks, batches and forwarded loggers. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a stuck Promise is abandoned after about 3 seconds and reported with `LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE`.
Resolves when the known work finished or the budget ran out.
onShutdown: Registers a cleanup handler run at the start of `shutdown()`; it may still write final logs.
onShutdown.fn: `(reason) => void | Promise<void>`; `reason` is the value passed to `shutdown()`.
shutdown: Closes the logger: runs shutdown handlers, flushes, then uninstalls all plugins. Reentrant and concurrent calls share the same Promise. Afterwards logs are silently ignored and the logger cannot be reopened.
shutdown.reason: Why it closes: `manual` from application code; `signal`, `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection` are passed by `process()`.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult` from `@migaia/plugin-host`; `cleanupErrors` lists plugin cleanup failures. A clock failure rejects this same published completion after attempting Host cleanup, retaining primary and cleanup causes. Persistent clock failure can also defeat the Host budget; cleanup or receipt success does not promise remote delivery.
dispose: Same as `shutdown("manual")`.
The disposal result of `shutdown()`.
use: Installs plugins after construction (also async ones), through the same checks as constructor plugins. Each call must use new plugin objects.
use.plugins: Plugin objects created by factories such as `level()` or `http(config)`.
A tuple of plugin handles in input order; `handle.extensions` holds the API the plugin added.
unUse: Uninstalls a plugin by name and releases what it registered (stages, sinks, hooks, flush and shutdown callbacks).
unUse.name: Plugin name, such as `LEVEL_PLUGIN_NAME` (`level`).
Resolves after the plugin is removed.
extends: Forwards every entry, after this logger processed it, through the whole pipeline and sinks of each target (their level filters apply). Self or cyclic forwarding throws `EXTENDS_SELF` / `EXTENDS_CYCLE`.
extends.others: Target loggers created by `new Logger()`.
This logger, for chaining.
unextend: Removes forwarding edges to the given loggers; the targets are not closed.
unextend.others: Loggers previously passed to `extends()`.
`true` when at least one edge was removed.
onDispose: Inside a plugin `install(core)` only: registers a cleanup run when the plugin is uninstalled.
onDispose.resource: A disposer function or an object with `dispose()`.
Nothing; the cleanup is registered.

members.description: Plugins read their own configuration through `core.config.get<TConfig>()`, not `this.config`. This scoped reader exposes the host-owned snapshot without a plugin-name argument. Keeping reads at the core boundary makes plugin configuration available to host diagnostics.

members.name: scheduler
members.description: The logger's monotonic clock source (R-9). `flush`, `shutdown`, batch deadlines, and `boundedWait` use this scheduler. Defaults to utils/scheduler `systemScheduler`. Plugins use it to share the host's clock domain.

members.description: Dispatches explicit entry fields such as `meta`, `data`, and `context`.

members.name: usePipeline
members.description: Registers a pipeline stage that can transform an entry, forward it with `next`, or drop it by omitting `next`. Supported methods follow the middleware-pipeline promotion table. Sync stages run in any mode. Generator stages also promote to `async-generator`. Other stages require their matching mode. An unresolved mode union retains all methods and leaves validation to runtime admission.

members.name: useSink
members.description: Registers a sink. Every registered sink processes entries that pass the full pipeline, such as console and HTTP sinks together.

members.name: hook
members.description: Registers a named lifecycle hook. Built-in names are `before`, `after`, `before:${tag}`, and `after:${tag}`. Plugins can also define their own hook names.

members.name: onFailure
members.description: Observes asynchronous output failures without changing normal log-call control flow.

members.name: defer
members.description: Schedules work outside the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager. `flush` and `shutdown` wait for this work. Plugins configured for async output use this path for rendering, stdout writes, or network requests.

members.name: onFlush
members.description: Registers a callback to empty a buffer during `flush()`. The core invokes these callbacks and also waits for unfinished `defer()` tasks and Promises returned by sinks. For example, an HTTP sink without batching still keeps each pending request in the drain wait.

members.name: onShutdown
members.description: Shutdown disposes installed plugins after draining; subsequent log calls are ignored.

members.name: dispose
members.description: Returns the same terminal completion as shutdown(manual).

members.name: raw
members.description: Writes raw text to stdout without passing through the pipeline or sinks. `asyncOutput: true` schedules the write through `defer`. Streaming plugins such as reasoning use this for token output without a complete log format per token.

members.name: extends
members.signature: extends(...others: readonly Omit<ILoggerCore<TMode, TShared>, 'config' | 'onDispose'>[]): ILoggerCore<TMode, TShared>;
members.description: Forwards entries to the full pipelines and sinks of each target after the current logger processes them. After `log1.extends(log2, log3)`, target level thresholds and filters still apply to forwarded entries. Each forwarding hop records its topic in internal forwarding state carried in `entry.data`. Registration detects cycles using logger context IDs. Runtime forwarding also skips IDs already present in the internal forwarding path. This composes forwarding behavior, not plugin extension types. The returned logger keeps the current logger's TypeScript capabilities; target-only methods are not added.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
config: Configuration store of the installed plugins. On a logger it is `ILoggerConfig` (`get(path)`, `update(name, recipe)`); inside a plugin `install(core)` it is a reader of that plugin configuration only (`get()`).
ctx: Frozen context of this logger: `id`, application `options`, default context `path`, `topic`, `createdAt` and `env`.
scheduler: Clock and timers used by `flush()`, `shutdown()` and batch deadlines; the `scheduler` option or `systemScheduler`.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs) captured at construction from the `runtimeManager` option or `getLoggerRuntimeManager()`; plugins use the same object.
log: Console-style entry point: builds an entry with this tag and message and dispatches it through pipeline, hooks and sinks. A trailing object stays an argument; it is not turned into `meta`. Never throws for sink failures.
log.tag: Entry tag such as `info` or `audit`; `level()` filters standard level tags.
log.message: Message text; `%s`, `%d`, `%o` placeholders are left for the console sink.
log.args: Extra values stored in `entry.args` in order.
No value. Shutdown handlers can still enqueue final structured entries; calls are ignored after draining closes dispatch admission.
dispatchRaw: Dispatches an entry with explicit fields (`meta`, `data`, `context`, `error`, `time`) for structured or audit logs.
dispatchRaw.input: `{ tag, message, args?, meta?, data?, context?, error?, time? }`; `context` defaults to the `context` option.
dispatchRaw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing; failures go to `onFailure()`.
raw: Writes text straight to stdout (or `console.log` without `process`), skipping pipeline and sinks; used for streaming output. Ignored once shutdown starts.
raw.text: Text passed unchanged to runtimeManager.write. A host stdout writer can preserve no-newline output; the default console.log fallback without process adds its own newline.
raw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing.
usePipeline: Registers a synchronous stage (entry, next, context?) => void in every pipeline mode. PluginHost lifts it into the selected mode; call next(entry) to continue or omit next to drop the entry.
usePipeline.stage: The stage function; call `next` at most once.
The same logger for chaining; synchronous registration works in all modes. Other stage registration methods follow the mode compatibility matrix.
useAsyncPipeline: Registers an async onion-style stage (mode `async` only): code after `await next(entry)` runs once the downstream finished.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (entry, next) => void`.
The same logger; other modes reject it at type level and at runtime.
useGeneratorPipeline: Registers a generator stage (modes `generator` and `async-generator`).
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: Generator (entry, context?), with optional pipeline context as the second argument, never next. Return a payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE after yielding to continue; an implicit undefined return halts.
The same logger, for chaining.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Registers an async generator stage (mode `async-generator` only); each stage runs to its final value before the next.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: Async generator (entry, context?) with optional context as the second argument. Yield stores a candidate; return payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE to continue. The logger explicitly delegates stage registration to its functional Host.
useSink: Registers an output that receives every entry passing the pipeline. Each sink gets its own shallow copy; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`; a throw goes to `onFailure()` with source `sink`.
useSink.sink: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`.
A function that removes only this registration; calling it again does nothing.
hook: Registers a hook under a name: built-in `before`, `after`, `before:<tag>`, `after:<tag>`, or a name a plugin fires. Hooks receive the live entry and may change it.
hook.name: Hook name.
hook.fn: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`.
An idempotent off callback removing only this registration; registering the same function again creates an independent subscription.
fireHook: Runs every hook registered under `name` with the given entry now.
fireHook.name: Hook name to fire.
fireHook.entry: An entry, usually received in a sink or stage.
Nothing; hook failures go to `onFailure()`.
onFailure: Observes failures of sinks, hooks, pipeline, deferred tasks, flush, forwarding and shutdown. Logging calls never throw them, so register this in production. If the terminal runtime reporter throws, rejects or has a throwing then getter, the existing Utils host exception queue exposes that failure without recursion or changing the business result.
onFailure.fn: `({ source, error }) => void`; see `ILogFailure`.
defer: Runs a task after the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager; `flush()` and `shutdown()` wait for it.
defer.task: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
Nothing; the task is scheduled, not awaited.
onFlush: Registers a callback that empties a buffer on every `flush()`.
onFlush.fn: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
flush: Waits for deferred tasks, async sink results, `onFlush` callbacks, batches and forwarded loggers. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a stuck Promise is abandoned after about 3 seconds and reported with `LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE`.
Resolves when the known work finished or the budget ran out.
onShutdown: Registers a cleanup handler run at the start of `shutdown()`; it may still write final logs.
onShutdown.fn: `(reason) => void | Promise<void>`; `reason` is the value passed to `shutdown()`.
shutdown: Closes the logger: runs shutdown handlers, flushes, then uninstalls all plugins. Reentrant and concurrent calls share the same Promise. Afterwards logs are silently ignored and the logger cannot be reopened.
shutdown.reason: Why it closes: `manual` from application code; `signal`, `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection` are passed by `process()`.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult` from `@migaia/plugin-host`; `cleanupErrors` lists plugin cleanup failures. A clock failure rejects this same published completion after attempting Host cleanup, retaining primary and cleanup causes. Persistent clock failure can also defeat the Host budget; cleanup or receipt success does not promise remote delivery.
dispose: Same as `shutdown("manual")`.
The disposal result of `shutdown()`.
use: Installs plugins after construction (also async ones), through the same checks as constructor plugins. Each call must use new plugin objects.
use.plugins: Plugin objects created by factories such as `level()` or `http(config)`.
A tuple of plugin handles in input order; `handle.extensions` holds the API the plugin added.
unUse: Uninstalls a plugin by name and releases what it registered (stages, sinks, hooks, flush and shutdown callbacks).
unUse.name: Plugin name, such as `LEVEL_PLUGIN_NAME` (`level`).
Resolves after the plugin is removed.
extends: Forwards every entry, after this logger processed it, through the whole pipeline and sinks of each target (their level filters apply). Self or cyclic forwarding throws `EXTENDS_SELF` / `EXTENDS_CYCLE`.
extends.others: Target loggers created by `new Logger()`.
This logger, for chaining.
unextend: Removes forwarding edges to the given loggers; the targets are not closed.
unextend.others: Loggers previously passed to `extends()`.
`true` when at least one edge was removed.
onDispose: Inside a plugin `install(core)` only: registers a cleanup run when the plugin is uninstalled.
onDispose.resource: A disposer function or an object with `dispose()`.
Nothing; the cleanup is registered.

id: Entry id `log_<n>`, increasing within the process.
tag: Tag of the entry, such as `audit`.
time: Creation time; a replacement entry must keep a `Date` of the current realm.
message: Message text of the entry.
args: Extra values passed after the message.
meta: Structured metadata given to `dispatchRaw()`.

symbols.name: Logger
symbols.signature: export declare const Logger: IStaticLoggerCtor;
symbols.purpose: Creates a logger. Plugins in `plugins` are installed synchronously in array order; a plugin whose install returns a Promise makes the constructor throw (install those later with `use()`). The methods of installed plugins appear on the instance with full types.
symbols.core:
options: Construction options; see `ILoggerOptions` (`execution` is required).
A logger instance; invalid options throw `INVALID_OPTION`, a failing plugin rolls back the plugins installed before it and rethrows.
config: Configuration store of the installed plugins. On a logger it is `ILoggerConfig` (`get(path)`, `update(name, recipe)`); inside a plugin `install(core)` it is a reader of that plugin configuration only (`get()`).
ctx: Frozen context of this logger: `id`, application `options`, default context `path`, `topic`, `createdAt` and `env`.
scheduler: Clock and timers used by `flush()`, `shutdown()` and batch deadlines; the `scheduler` option or `systemScheduler`.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs) captured at construction from the `runtimeManager` option or `getLoggerRuntimeManager()`; plugins use the same object.
log: Console-style entry point: builds an entry with this tag and message and dispatches it through pipeline, hooks and sinks. A trailing object stays an argument; it is not turned into `meta`. Never throws for sink failures.
log.tag: Entry tag such as `info` or `audit`; `level()` filters standard level tags.
log.message: Message text; `%s`, `%d`, `%o` placeholders are left for the console sink.
log.args: Extra values stored in `entry.args` in order.
No value. Shutdown handlers can still enqueue final structured entries; calls are ignored after draining closes dispatch admission.
dispatchRaw: Dispatches an entry with explicit fields (`meta`, `data`, `context`, `error`, `time`) for structured or audit logs.
dispatchRaw.input: `{ tag, message, args?, meta?, data?, context?, error?, time? }`; `context` defaults to the `context` option.
dispatchRaw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing; failures go to `onFailure()`.
raw: Writes text straight to stdout (or `console.log` without `process`), skipping pipeline and sinks; used for streaming output. Ignored once shutdown starts.
raw.text: Text passed unchanged to runtimeManager.write. A host stdout writer can preserve no-newline output; the default console.log fallback without process adds its own newline.
raw.options: Optional `{ asyncOutput }`: `true` schedules the output with `defer()` so the call returns before any sink runs; default `false`.
Nothing.
usePipeline: Registers a synchronous stage (entry, next, context?) => void in every pipeline mode. PluginHost lifts it into the selected mode; call next(entry) to continue or omit next to drop the entry.
usePipeline.stage: The stage function; call `next` at most once.
The same logger for chaining; synchronous registration works in all modes. Other stage registration methods follow the mode compatibility matrix.
useAsyncPipeline: Registers an async onion-style stage (mode `async` only): code after `await next(entry)` runs once the downstream finished.
useAsyncPipeline.stage: `async (entry, next) => void`.
The same logger; other modes reject it at type level and at runtime.
useGeneratorPipeline: Registers a generator stage (modes `generator` and `async-generator`).
useGeneratorPipeline.stage: Generator (entry, context?), with optional pipeline context as the second argument, never next. Return a payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE after yielding to continue; an implicit undefined return halts.
The same logger, for chaining.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline: Registers an async generator stage (mode `async-generator` only); each stage runs to its final value before the next.
useAsyncGeneratorPipeline.stage: Async generator (entry, context?) with optional context as the second argument. Yield stores a candidate; return payload or GENERATOR_CONTINUE to continue. The logger explicitly delegates stage registration to its functional Host.
useSink: Registers an output that receives every entry passing the pipeline. Each sink gets its own shallow copy; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`; a throw goes to `onFailure()` with source `sink`.
useSink.sink: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`.
A function that removes only this registration; calling it again does nothing.
hook: Registers a hook under a name: built-in `before`, `after`, `before:<tag>`, `after:<tag>`, or a name a plugin fires. Hooks receive the live entry and may change it.
hook.name: Hook name.
hook.fn: `(entry) => void | Promise<void>`; a returned Promise is awaited by `flush()`.
An idempotent off callback removing only this registration; registering the same function again creates an independent subscription.
fireHook: Runs every hook registered under `name` with the given entry now.
fireHook.name: Hook name to fire.
fireHook.entry: An entry, usually received in a sink or stage.
Nothing; hook failures go to `onFailure()`.
onFailure: Observes failures of sinks, hooks, pipeline, deferred tasks, flush, forwarding and shutdown. Logging calls never throw them, so register this in production. If the terminal runtime reporter throws, rejects or has a throwing then getter, the existing Utils host exception queue exposes that failure without recursion or changing the business result.
onFailure.fn: `({ source, error }) => void`; see `ILogFailure`.
defer: Runs a task after the current synchronous stack through the runtime manager; `flush()` and `shutdown()` wait for it.
defer.task: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
Nothing; the task is scheduled, not awaited.
onFlush: Registers a callback that empties a buffer on every `flush()`.
onFlush.fn: `() => void | Promise<void>`.
flush: Waits for deferred tasks, async sink results, `onFlush` callbacks, batches and forwarded loggers. Concurrent calls share one Promise; a stuck Promise is abandoned after about 3 seconds and reported with `LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE`.
Resolves when the known work finished or the budget ran out.
onShutdown: Registers a cleanup handler run at the start of `shutdown()`; it may still write final logs.
onShutdown.fn: `(reason) => void | Promise<void>`; `reason` is the value passed to `shutdown()`.
shutdown: Closes the logger: runs shutdown handlers, flushes, then uninstalls all plugins. Reentrant and concurrent calls share the same Promise. Afterwards logs are silently ignored and the logger cannot be reopened.
shutdown.reason: Why it closes: `manual` from application code; `signal`, `uncaughtException`, `unhandledRejection` are passed by `process()`.
An `IPluginHostDisposalResult` from `@migaia/plugin-host`; `cleanupErrors` lists plugin cleanup failures. A clock failure rejects this same published completion after attempting Host cleanup, retaining primary and cleanup causes. Persistent clock failure can also defeat the Host budget; cleanup or receipt success does not promise remote delivery.
dispose: Same as `shutdown("manual")`.
The disposal result of `shutdown()`.
use: Installs plugins after construction (also async ones), through the same checks as constructor plugins. Each call must use new plugin objects.
use.plugins: Plugin objects created by factories such as `level()` or `http(config)`.
A tuple of plugin handles in input order; `handle.extensions` holds the API the plugin added.
unUse: Uninstalls a plugin by name and releases what it registered (stages, sinks, hooks, flush and shutdown callbacks).
unUse.name: Plugin name, such as `LEVEL_PLUGIN_NAME` (`level`).
Resolves after the plugin is removed.
extends: Forwards every entry, after this logger processed it, through the whole pipeline and sinks of each target (their level filters apply). Self or cyclic forwarding throws `EXTENDS_SELF` / `EXTENDS_CYCLE`.
extends.others: Target loggers created by `new Logger()`.
This logger, for chaining.
unextend: Removes forwarding edges to the given loggers; the targets are not closed.
unextend.others: Loggers previously passed to `extends()`.
`true` when at least one edge was removed.
onDispose: Inside a plugin `install(core)` only: registers a cleanup run when the plugin is uninstalled.
onDispose.resource: A disposer function or an object with `dispose()`.
Nothing; the cleanup is registered.
execution: Required deadlines: `mutationTimeoutMs` for plugin install/uninstall and `pipelineDrainTimeoutMs` for pipeline drain; `false` means no deadline.
runtimeManager: Host capabilities this logger uses (stdout, UUID, scheduling, fetch, fs).
The manager returned by `getLoggerRuntimeManager()` at construction.
context: Default context path of entries that do not pass `context`.
`[]`: no context.
topic: Name of this logger in the forwarding chain shown by `extends()`.
`""`: not shown.
on: Hooks registered at construction, same as calling `hook(name, fn)` for each key.
`{}`: no hooks.
plugins: Plugins installed synchronously in array order; their methods appear on the instance.
`[]`: a bare core with `log()` only.
options: Application settings frozen and exposed to plugins as `core.ctx.options`.
`{}`.
pipeline: Pipeline settings; `mode` is fixed at construction.
`{ mode: "sync" }`.
pipeline.mode: How pipeline stages run; it decides which `use*Pipeline` method is accepted.
`sync`.
Stages run one after another synchronously; register with `usePipeline`.
Onion model: `await next()` waits for the downstream; register with `useAsyncPipeline`.
Generator stages; register with `useGeneratorPipeline`.
Async generator stages, each awaited to its final value; register with `useAsyncGeneratorPipeline`.
scheduler: Clock and timers for flush, shutdown and batch deadlines; inject a manual scheduler in tests.
`systemScheduler` from `@migaia/utils/scheduler`.
symbols.advanced:
One logging API across Node, Bun, Deno, browsers and workers, with only the plugins each environment needs.
Production pipelines that batch and upload entries, and must not lose them on exit (`flush()`, `shutdown()`).
Forwarding one logger into another (`extends()`), for example a module logger into an audit logger.
Sharing one plugin object between loggers: create a new one per logger (`level()` twice), otherwise their state is mixed.
parameters: This const declaration has no parameters.

examples:
import { Logger, setLoggerRuntimeManager } from '@migaia/logger'
import { batch, color, http, level, process, reasoning, uuid } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  context: ['app', 'api'],
  topic: 'gateway',
  options: { service: 'gateway' },
  on: { before: (entry) => {} },
  pipeline: { mode: 'sync' },
  plugins: [level(), color()]
})

import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { file } from '@migaia/logger/plugins/file'

const logger = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [file({ path: 'logs/app.jsonl', batch: { maxSize: 20 } })]
})
logger.log('info', 'ready')
await logger.flush()
await logger.shutdown('manual')

import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { batch, color, http, level, process, uuid } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  context: ['worker'],
  plugins: [
    level({ level: 'info' }),
    uuid({ display: true }),
    batch({ maxSize: 50, maxWaitMs: 1000 }),
    http({ url: 'https://logs.example/v1/entries', batch: { maxSize: 50 } }),
    color({ format: 'pretty' }),
    process()
  ]
})

log.onFailure(({ source, error }) => reportLoggerFailure(source, error))
log.info('job started', { jobId: 'j_1' })
await log.flush()

import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { color, level } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  context: ['api'],
  plugins: [level({ level: 'info' }), color({ format: 'pretty', color: 'auto' })]
})

log.info('server listening on %d', 3000)
log.error('request failed', new Error('timeout'))

await log.flush() // 确保上面这些日志真正落地了再退出/继续

import { Logger } from '@migaia/logger'
import { batch, http, level, process } from '@migaia/logger/plugins'

const log = new Logger({
  execution: { mutationTimeoutMs: false, pipelineDrainTimeoutMs: false },
  plugins: [
    level({ level: 'info' }),
    batch({ maxSize: 50, maxWaitMs: 1000 }),
    http({ url: 'https://logs.example/v1/entries', batch: { maxSize: 50 } }),
    process() // 进程退出/崩溃前自动 flush
  ]
})

log.onFailure(({ source, error }) => console.error(`[logger] ${source} failed`, error))

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
One logging API across Node, Bun, Deno, browsers and workers, with only the plugins each environment needs.
Production pipelines that batch and upload entries, and must not lose them on exit (`flush()`, `shutdown()`).
Forwarding one logger into another (`extends()`), for example a module logger into an audit logger.
Sharing one plugin object between loggers: create a new one per logger (`level()` twice), otherwise their state is mixed.

blocks.text: 1. 构造函数只接受同步安装的插件。`new Logger({ plugins: [...] })` 里的插件必须能同步完成安装，需要异步安装的插件用 `await log.use(plugin)`。 2. 插件实例不能跨 logger 复用。每次安装都应该重新调用一次插件工厂函数（`level()`、`http()` 等），不要把同一个插件实例装到多个 `Logger`，否则内部状态可能串联。 3. `shutdown()` 之后日志被静默忽略，不会抛错也不会有任何提示——这是有意的（避免退出流程里到处加判断），需要感知的话订阅 `onFailure()` 或自行检查状态。 4. 日志系统内部的失败不会从业务调用抛出。`log.info()` 永远不会因为 sink 挂了而抛异常——务必用 `onFailure()` 观察，否则问题会悄悄消失。 5. `pipeline.mode` 构造后不可切换。sync stage 可提升到任意模式，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其余不兼容组合会立即报 `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`，详见 USEGUIDE。 6. `http()` 通过 Feature 解析 batch provider：同批 `[batch(), http(...)]` 或反序均按依赖排序；跨调用晚装 batch 不会追溯重绑。 7. `extends()` 只转发运行时输出路径，不会把目标 logger 的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并进当前变量的类型。 8. 批处理队列有界且不会静默丢日志：`maxPendingBatches` 默认 `1024`，满载时抛出/上报 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；生产环境应通过 `onFailure()` 监控并在下游恢复后再接纳新日志。

invalidOption: `INVALID_OPTION`: an option is unreadable or invalid; fix it (`cause` keeps the getter error).
pipelineEntryInvalid: `PIPELINE_ENTRY_INVALID`: a stage replaced the entry without a valid `Date`; the original entry is delivered.
runtimeShuttingDown: `RUNTIME_SHUTTING_DOWN`: `process()` or a logger was installed while the process is shutting down.
pluginConfigConflict: `PLUGIN_CONFIG_CONFLICT`: `process()` installed again with a different configuration.
transportUnavailable: `TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE`: `http()` found no `fetch`; inject one in the runtime manager.
serializeFailed: `SERIALIZE_FAILED`: entries could not be turned into JSON; see `cause`.
deliveryFailed: `DELIVERY_FAILED`: upload got a failure response or ran out of retries, or a file write failed.
invalidRetryCount: `INVALID_RETRY_COUNT`: `retries` is not a finite non-negative integer.
lifecycleDeadline: `LIFECYCLE_DEADLINE`: flush or shutdown reached its deadline with work left; delivery is not guaranteed.
processInstallRollbackFailed: `PROCESS_INSTALL_ROLLBACK_FAILED`: `process()` install failed and removing its listeners failed too; read `errors`.
pluginUninstallCleanupFailed: `PLUGIN_UNINSTALL_CLEANUP_FAILED`: some cleanup of an uninstalled plugin failed; read `cause` / `errors`.
pluginShutdownCleanupFailed: `PLUGIN_SHUTDOWN_CLEANUP_FAILED`: cleanup during shutdown or exit failed; the primary error is kept.
hookFailed: `HOOK_FAILED`: an `onFailure` callback itself threw; reported to the console only, never thrown.
extendsSelf: `EXTENDS_SELF`: a logger was forwarded to itself.
extendsCycle: `EXTENDS_CYCLE`: a new `extends()` edge would form a cycle.
batchOverflow: `BATCH_OVERFLOW`: the pending batch limit was reached and the oldest queued batch was dropped.
fileSinkUnavailable: `FILE_SINK_UNAVAILABLE`: `file()` has no injected `fs` and no Node default.

members.name: invalidOption
members.description: Logger construction received an unreadable or structurally invalid public option. The caller * must fix the option; the native `TypeError` keeps the original accessor failure in `cause` when * one exists. Also rejects shutdown clock failure after admitted plugin cleanup has run.

members.name: pipelineEntryInvalid
members.description: A pipeline supplied a replacement without a current-realm Date time. Dispatch reports this * native TypeError and keeps delivering the original entry; the plugin must preserve its Date.

members.name: runtimeShuttingDown
members.description: Process plugin/logger installation is attempted while runtime shutdown is already in progress. * Enforces logger SDD §4.3 and §5.1: shutdown admission is terminal for that runtime. The caller * must wait for shutdown to settle or install the logger without the process plugin.

members.name: pluginConfigConflict
members.description: Thrown when the process plugin is installed again with a different configuration. * * Use the same configuration or uninstall the plugin before reinstalling.

members.name: transportUnavailable
members.description: Thrown when the host runtime has no HTTP transport (`fetch`). * * Supply a runtime manager with `fetch` or use the HTTP plugin on a host that supports fetch.

members.name: serializeFailed
members.description: Thrown when serializing HTTP log entries fails. * * `cause` retains the original serialization error. Inspect the logged payload.

members.name: deliveryFailed
members.description: HTTP delivery receives a non-success response or exhausts retryable transport attempts. * Enforces logger SDD §4.5 and §5.3 (LG-R6-4/LG-R18); callers must inspect the endpoint/transport * and apply their own delivery remediation while logger failure policy contains the sink * failure.

members.name: invalidRetryCount
members.description: HTTP plugin construction receives a retry count that is not a finite non-negative integer. * Enforces logger SDD §4.5 (LG-R6-8); callers must correct the plugin configuration before * constructing or installing the logger.

members.name: lifecycleDeadline
members.description: A bounded logger flush or shutdown phase reaches its absolute deadline with work unfinished. * Enforces logger SDD §4.2 and §5.2 (LG-R6-5); callers must treat delivery as degraded and * inspect the reported pending work instead of assuming every entry was delivered.

members.name: processInstallRollbackFailed
members.description: Process plugin installation fails and listener rollback reports one or more additional errors. * Enforces logger SDD §4.3 and §5.3 (LG-R11); callers must inspect `AggregateError.errors`, fix * the primary installation failure, and verify runtime listeners before retrying installation.

members.name: pluginUninstallCleanupFailed
members.description: Logger plugin final uninstall cleanup attempted every registered action but one or more actions * failed. Enforces logger SDD LG-R23/LG-R24 and §5.5; callers must inspect the cause or * `AggregateError.errors` and may create a fresh plugin instance after runtime state resets. A * batcher whose final drain left entries undelivered reports this code with `detail.dropped`.

members.name: pluginShutdownCleanupFailed
members.description: Logger shutdown cleanup failed while cancelling a deadline task or invoking the captured exit * path. Enforces logger SDD LG-R24 and §5.5; callers must inspect the primary and cleanup errors * before deciding whether the process can continue.

members.name: hookFailed
members.description: Diagnostic code reported when a failure hook throws. It is not thrown itself. * * The reporter uses only `runtime.console.error` or `runtime.write`, preventing recursive failure * reporting.

members.name: extendsSelf
members.description: Thrown when `extends()` receives the current logger itself. * * Do not add a logger to its own forwarding targets.

members.name: extendsCycle
members.description: Thrown when `extends()` would create a forwarding cycle. The target logger can already forward * through its own targets back to the current logger. * * Inspect the forwarding graph and remove the cycle.

members.name: batchOverflow
members.description: A bounded batch/direct-HTTP owner had no admission slot for another full batch, so it dropped * the oldest queued batch (or the incoming one when every pending batch is in flight). Reported * through the logger failure path, not thrown to the producer; `detail.dropped` is the dropped * entry count. Callers should raise `maxPendingBatches` or relieve the slow batch callback.

members.name: fileSinkUnavailable
members.description: File plugin installation found neither an injected file-system capability nor the supported * Node default. Enforces R1 BZ35; callers must inject `fs` or use the Node condition.

symbols.purpose: Plugin adding no logger methods; it provides batching for HTTP and file consumers. Same-batch plugins are sorted by Feature dependencies, independent of array order; a provider installed in a later use call does not retroactively rebind consumers.

A plugin object for one logger.
maxSize: Sends a batch as soon as it holds this many entries.
`20`.
maxWaitMs: Sends a non-empty batch at most this many milliseconds after its first entry arrived.
`2000`.
maxConcurrentBatches: How many batch callbacks may run at once; a positive safe integer.
`1`: batches are delivered one after another, in order.
maxPendingBatches: Limit of queued plus running batches. When full, the oldest queued batch is dropped and `BATCH_OVERFLOW` (with the dropped count) is reported to `onFailure()`.
`1024`.
flushTimeoutMs: Time budget of one batch drain during `flush()` and uninstall; entries still waiting afterwards are reported as not delivered.
`3000`.
asyncOutput: Runs a size-triggered batch callback through `defer()` instead of inside the logging call.
`true`.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxConcurrentBatches
declaredConfiguration.description: Maximum number of batches executing at once. Defaults to one for lossless delivery.

declaredConfiguration.name: maxPendingBatches
declaredConfiguration.description: Maximum number of queued or executing batches. Defaults to 1024. A full batch beyond it drops the oldest queued batch and reports `BATCH_OVERFLOW` with `detail.dropped`.

declaredConfiguration.name: flushTimeoutMs
declaredConfiguration.description: Time budget in milliseconds for one `flush()` drain, including the drain on dispose. Defaults to 3000. Entries still buffered or queued when dispose reaches it are dropped and reported.

declaredConfiguration.name: asyncOutput
declaredConfiguration.description: Schedules a full-batch callback asynchronously when enabled. Defaults to `true`; timer-triggered callbacks are already asynchronous.

blocks.text: 1. 构造函数只接受同步安装的插件。`new Logger({ plugins: [...] })` 里的插件必须能同步完成安装，需要异步安装的插件用 `await log.use(plugin)`。 2. 插件实例不能跨 logger 复用。每次安装都应该重新调用一次插件工厂函数（`level()`、`http()` 等），不要把同一个插件实例装到多个 `Logger`，否则内部状态可能串联。 3. `shutdown()` 之后日志被静默忽略，不会抛错也不会有任何提示——这是有意的（避免退出流程里到处加判断），需要感知的话订阅 `onFailure()` 或自行检查状态。 4. 日志系统内部的失败不会从业务调用抛出。`log.info()` 永远不会因为 sink 挂了而抛异常——务必用 `onFailure()` 观察，否则问题会悄悄消失。 5. `pipeline.mode` 构造后不可切换。sync stage 可提升到任意模式，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其余不兼容组合会立即报 `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`，详见 USEGUIDE。 6. `http()` 通过 Feature 解析 batch provider：同批 `[batch(), http(...)]` 或反序均按依赖排序；跨调用晚装 batch 不会追溯重绑。 7. `extends()` 只转发运行时输出路径，不会把目标 logger 的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并进当前变量的类型。 8. 批处理队列有界且不会静默丢日志：`maxPendingBatches` 默认 `1024`，满载时抛出/上报 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；生产环境应通过 `onFailure()` 监控并在下游恢复后再接纳新日志。

rows: 网络错误、429、5xx 情况下的额外重试次数。
单次请求最长等待时间；超时会 abort 当前请求并按网络错误处理。
覆盖传给 `batch()` shared factory 的配置。

blocks.text: 4xx 错误（429 除外）会直接失败、不重试；429 优先读取响应的 `Retry-After` 头部作为等待时间，没有该头部时退回指数退避。关闭先排空最终日志，再在 HTTP 插件释放时 abort 剩余请求；失败由 `onFailure()` 观察。同一批安装的 batch/http 按 Feature 依赖排序，`[http(...), batch()]` 同样生效；跨 use 调用晚装 provider 不会追溯重绑。没有 batch provider 时，指定 http.batch 仍启用本地有界队列，但强制 maxSize:1、asyncOutput:false。
所有 Logger 自有错误都带 `source: '@migaia/logger'` 与下列稳定 `code`；业务日志入口通常不直接抛出 sink/plugin 失败，应通过 `onFailure()` 观察。

rows: 公开配置不可读或结构非法；修正配置，getter 原错误保留在 `cause`
pipeline 替换值的 time 非当前 realm Date；报告后交付原 entry
runtime 已进入 shutdown 后仍安装 process/logger；等待终结或不要安装 process plugin
process plugin 以不同配置重复安装；统一配置或卸载后重装
http plugin 找不到 `fetch`；注入 runtime fetch 或换宿主
HTTP payload 序列化失败；检查 `cause` 与待记录数据
非成功响应或可重试传输耗尽；检查 endpoint/网络并由业务决定补偿
retries 不是有限非负整数；构造前修正
flush/shutdown 到达绝对截止时间仍有工作；按降级交付处理，不要假设全部送达
process 安装失败且 listener 回滚也失败；展开 `AggregateError.errors`
plugin 最终卸载清理失败；检查 `cause`/`errors`，实例视为终结
shutdown 的 deadline task 或退出清理失败；保留 primary 与 cleanup 错误
failure hook 自身失败的诊断码；只走 runtime reporter，不递归抛给业务入口
logger 转发给自身；移除自引用
新 extends 边形成环；拆除环路
pending 满载：丢最老排队批次，全在途时丢新批次；检查 dropped 并按业务补偿
file 插件无注入的 `fs` 能力且无 Node 默认能力；注入 `fs` 或选择 Node 条件

blocks.text: 1. 构造函数只接受同步安装的插件。`new Logger({ plugins: [...] })` 里的插件必须能同步完成安装，需要异步安装的插件用 `await log.use(plugin)`。 2. 插件实例不能跨 logger 复用。每次安装都应该重新调用一次插件工厂函数（`level()`、`http()` 等），不要把同一个插件实例装到多个 `Logger`，否则内部状态可能串联。 3. `shutdown()` 之后日志被静默忽略，不会抛错也不会有任何提示——这是有意的（避免退出流程里到处加判断），需要感知的话订阅 `onFailure()` 或自行检查状态。 4. 日志系统内部的失败不会从业务调用抛出。`log.info()` 永远不会因为 sink 挂了而抛异常——务必用 `onFailure()` 观察，否则问题会悄悄消失。 5. `pipeline.mode` 构造后不可切换。sync stage 可提升到任意模式，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其余不兼容组合会立即报 `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`，详见 USEGUIDE。 6. `http()` 通过 Feature 解析 batch provider：同批 `[batch(), http(...)]` 或反序均按依赖排序；跨调用晚装 batch 不会追溯重绑。 7. `extends()` 只转发运行时输出路径，不会把目标 logger 的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并进当前变量的类型。 8. 批处理队列有界且不会静默丢日志：`maxPendingBatches` 默认 `1024`，满载时抛出/上报 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；生产环境应通过 `onFailure()` 监控并在下游恢复后再接纳新日志。

flushTimeoutMs: Time budget of one batch drain during `flush()` and uninstall; entries still waiting afterwards are reported as not delivered.
`3000`.

blocks.text: `color` 会识别 `entry.data.silent === true` 并跳过打印这条 entry（但其他 sink，比如 HTTP，仍会正常接收它）——常用于"这条日志需要上报但不需要刷屏"的场景。

1. 构造函数只接受同步安装的插件。`new Logger({ plugins: [...] })` 里的插件必须能同步完成安装，需要异步安装的插件用 `await log.use(plugin)`。 2. 插件实例不能跨 logger 复用。每次安装都应该重新调用一次插件工厂函数（`level()`、`http()` 等），不要把同一个插件实例装到多个 `Logger`，否则内部状态可能串联。 3. `shutdown()` 之后日志被静默忽略，不会抛错也不会有任何提示——这是有意的（避免退出流程里到处加判断），需要感知的话订阅 `onFailure()` 或自行检查状态。 4. 日志系统内部的失败不会从业务调用抛出。`log.info()` 永远不会因为 sink 挂了而抛异常——务必用 `onFailure()` 观察，否则问题会悄悄消失。 5. `pipeline.mode` 构造后不可切换。sync stage 可提升到任意模式，generator stage 还可提升到 async-generator；其余不兼容组合会立即报 `PIPELINE_MODE_MISMATCH`，详见 USEGUIDE。 6. `http()` 通过 Feature 解析 batch provider：同批 `[batch(), http(...)]` 或反序均按依赖排序；跨调用晚装 batch 不会追溯重绑。 7. `extends()` 只转发运行时输出路径，不会把目标 logger 的 TypeScript 扩展方法合并进当前变量的类型。 8. 批处理队列有界且不会静默丢日志：`maxPendingBatches` 默认 `1024`，满载时抛出/上报 `BATCH_OVERFLOW`；生产环境应通过 `onFailure()` 监控并在下游恢复后再接纳新日志。

sections.title: 介绍
sections.content: Plugin that appends entries to a file as JSON lines, one batch per append, and can ask the injected `fs` to rotate the file. Write failures go to `onFailure()`.

sections.title: 上手
sections.content: Import file from @migaia/logger/plugins/file, then follow a maintained task example for your use case.

sections.title: 核心用法
sections.content:
config: Required; see `IFilePluginConfig` (`path` is required).
A plugin object; an empty `path` or invalid `rotate` limits throw `INVALID_OPTION`.
path: File the JSON lines are appended to; must not be empty.
batch: Batch settings; with `batch()` installed they are applied over its defaults.
Not set: the batch defaults (20 entries or 2 seconds).
batch.maxSize: Sends a batch as soon as it holds this many entries.
`20`.
batch.maxWaitMs: Sends a non-empty batch at most this many milliseconds after its first entry arrived.
`2000`.
batch.maxConcurrentBatches: How many batch callbacks may run at once; a positive safe integer.
`1`: batches are delivered one after another, in order.
batch.maxPendingBatches: Limit of queued plus running batches. When full, the oldest queued batch is dropped and `BATCH_OVERFLOW` (with the dropped count) is reported to `onFailure()`.
`1024`.
batch.flushTimeoutMs: Time budget of one batch drain during `flush()` and uninstall; entries still waiting afterwards are reported as not delivered.
`3000`.
batch.asyncOutput: Runs a size-triggered batch callback through `defer()` instead of inside the logging call.
`true`.
rotate: After appending a batch that reached a limit, call `runtimeManager.fs.rotate(path)`. The Node default `fs` has no `rotate`, so rotation needs an injected `fs`.
Not set: never rotate.
rotate.maxBytes: Rotate when one batch is at least this many UTF-8 bytes; a positive safe integer.
Not set: no byte limit.
rotate.maxEntries: Rotate when one batch holds at least this many entries; a positive safe integer.
Not set: no entry limit.
After installation every entry is appended to `path` as one JSON line, batch by batch, through `runtimeManager.fs` or the Node default. No methods are added; write failures reach `onFailure()` as `DELIVERY_FAILED`.

sections.title: 高阶用法
sections.content:
Installing without any `fs` capability fails; the install error carries `FILE_SINK_UNAVAILABLE` on `cause`.
Remaining entries are written on `flush()` and when the logger shuts down.
Keep local JSON-lines logs on a server or desktop app.

blocks.text: 所有 Logger 自有错误都带 `source: '@migaia/logger'` 与下列稳定 `code`；业务日志入口通常不直接抛出 sink/plugin 失败，应通过 `onFailure()` 观察。

rows: 公开配置不可读或结构非法；修正配置，getter 原错误保留在 `cause`
pipeline 替换值的 time 非当前 realm Date；报告后交付原 entry
runtime 已进入 shutdown 后仍安装 process/logger；等待终结或不要安装 process plugin
process plugin 以不同配置重复安装；统一配置或卸载后重装
http plugin 找不到 `fetch`；注入 runtime fetch 或换宿主
HTTP payload 序列化失败；检查 `cause` 与待记录数据
非成功响应或可重试传输耗尽；检查 endpoint/网络并由业务决定补偿
retries 不是有限非负整数；构造前修正
flush/shutdown 到达绝对截止时间仍有工作；按降级交付处理，不要假设全部送达
process 安装失败且 listener 回滚也失败；展开 `AggregateError.errors`
plugin 最终卸载清理失败；检查 `cause`/`errors`，实例视为终结
shutdown 的 deadline task 或退出清理失败；保留 primary 与 cleanup 错误
failure hook 自身失败的诊断码；只走 runtime reporter，不递归抛给业务入口
logger 转发给自身；移除自引用
新 extends 边形成环；拆除环路
pending 满载：丢最老排队批次，全在途时丢新批次；检查 dropped 并按业务补偿
file 插件无注入的 `fs` 能力且无 Node 默认能力；注入 `fs` 或选择 Node 条件

`2000`.

`1024`.
batch.flushTimeoutMs: Time budget of one batch drain during `flush()` and uninstall; entries still waiting afterwards are reported as not delivered.

rotate.maxBytes: Rotate when one batch is at least this many UTF-8 bytes; a positive safe integer.
